units.translation: (where χθόνα [the earth] was omitted by a printer's error in Poet. scen. p. 110a).

For thus Blomfield correctly wrote instead of ἄναγε μάν [up then] (in M άναγεμάν). In the same way Sophocles used ἄνα [up] for ἀνάστηθι [rise up] in the dactylic verse Ai. 194, on which see Lexicon Soph. p. 33b.

|| ἄνα [up] undergoes apocope in Suppl. 350 ἂμ πέτραις [on the rocks] and 550 Λύδιά τ᾽ ἂγ γύαλα [and Lydian glens], as Hermann corrected for metrical reasons instead of τε γύαλα [and glens], and in compounds ἀγκαλέομαι [I call upon], ἄγκρισις [judgment], ἀλλύτας [unloosed], άμβόαμα [I cry aloud], ἀμβοάω [I cry aloud], ἀμμίγνυμι [I mix], ἀμπέμπω [I send up], ἀμπίπτω [I fall upon], ἀμφαίνω [I show], ἀμφέρω [I carry about]. ἀνδαίω [I kindle], ἀντέλλω [I rise], ἀντολή [rising], ἀντρέπω [I overturn], and δυσάγκριτος [hard to judge].
and she wanders fasting along the seashore sand.
through the plains of Thrace and the wintry paths.
but those throughout the land of Asia, long called Asian (Meineke), are no longer ruled by Persians.
having gone up (thus Hermann for ἂν) always over the wandering-trodden earth.
they are dishonored throughout the city of the pious.
up then, houses (thus Hermann for δόμοις), rise up.

ἀγκαλέομαι [I call upon], ἄγκρισις [judgment], ἀλλύτας [unloosed], άμβόαμα [I cry aloud], ἀμβοάω [I cry aloud], ἀμμίγνυμι [I mix], ἀμπέμπω [I send up], ἀμπίπτω [I fall upon], ἀμφαίνω [I show], ἀμφέρω [I carry about]. ἀνδαίω [I kindle], ἀντέλλω [I rise], ἀντολή [rising], ἀντρέπω [I overturn], and δυσάγκριτος [hard to judge].
Thus κίνδυνον ἀναρρίπτειν [to throw the die of danger] is said.
I will bury him and take the danger upon myself.
to throw the die of danger
they came reporting oracles with shifting mouths.
[but it is pleasant to escape all that is necessary.]
and it is necessary to address.
ἀνάγκη [necessity] for ἀνάγκη ἐστί [it is necessary] means 'it is necessary'
Thus M and the scholia on this verse and on 465. In the Florentine copy ή τινος: whence Bothius proposed ἄλλαις ἀνάγκαις ἢ τινος τρέων κότον; [by other necessities or fearing someone's wrath?]
the strength of necessity is irresistible.
PR. But skill is far weaker than necessity. CH. Who then is the helmsman of necessity?
in the harsh whirlpools of necessity.
he entered the yoke-strap of necessity.
but if the necessity of this fate weighs down.
for the gods brought necessity that surrounds the city.
fearing the wrath of some other necessity?
nor may marriage come under compulsion.
I am yoked to these necessities, wretched.
they no longer pay tribute to despotic necessities.
and fawning under the necessities of the belly.
it is necessary to do these things.
nevertheless it is necessary to unfold all the suffering.
for what is without sense — it is necessary to nourish.
nevertheless it is necessary to revere the wrath of Zeus.
to raise a great war against either these or those is all necessity.
in any case it is necessary for me to have the courage for these things.
nevertheless it is necessary for mortals to bear misfortunes.
